title: Advancing Molecular Graph-Text Pre-training via Fine-grained Alignment

problem.claim: Molecular graph-text pre-training models need to learn both molecule-level and motif-level knowledge to support tasks requiring fine-grained molecular understanding.

gap.claim: Existing studies focus on whole molecular graphs and neglect motifs, limiting generalization to unseen molecules and motif-level tasks.

contributions.claim: FineMolTex is a molecular graph-text pre-training framework that jointly learns coarse-grained molecule-level and fine-grained motif-level knowledge.
FineMolTex combines contrastive alignment for coarse-grained matching with masked multi-modal modeling for fine-grained matching.
FineMolTex is evaluated across three downstream tasks and is reported to improve the text-based molecule editing task by up to 230%.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present FineMolTex as a novel fine-grained molecular graph-text pre-training framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across three downstream tasks, FineMolTex achieves up to 230% improvement in the text-based molecule editing task.
Case studies are reported to show that FineMolTex captures fine-grained knowledge.

narrative_sequence.summary: Molecular structure and related knowledge are important for scientific research, and recent work combines molecular graphs with textual descriptions.
Existing models neglect motifs, which are described as important for molecular properties, causing difficulty with unseen molecules and motif-level tasks.
FineMolTex jointly models molecule-level and motif-level knowledge through contrastive alignment and masked multi-modal modeling.
The authors report downstream-task improvements and case-study evidence of fine-grained knowledge capture.

source_observation.claim: The framework aligns coarse-grained and fine-grained information across molecular graph and text modalities.

interpretation.claim: Combining global alignment with importance-based local masking may help multimodal models represent domain-relevant substructures.

application.claim: Similar hierarchical alignment could be considered for other multimodal domains where local components carry task-relevant meaning.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this strategy improves all downstream tasks or transfers beyond molecular graph-text settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the three downstream tasks beyond naming text-based molecule editing.
The abstract does not provide baselines, datasets, evaluation metrics, or the exact meaning of the reported 230% improvement.
The abstract does not detail how motif and word importance are determined.
